articles.title: Newscast - Has Social Media For Children Just Changed Forever? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Tech giant Meta will pay up to $18billion to settle claims its platforms harm children
articles.body: Today, we discuss Meta’s decision to agree to an $18 billion settlement resolving claims from 29 US states that Facebook and Instagram harmed children. articles.title: Map: How much you pay in federal and state gas taxes as Trump weighs price cut
articles.summary: As national gas price averages head toward $5 per gallon, one state has already suspended its gas tax, and now President Donald Trump and his Cabinet are talking about doing the same.
articles.body: As national gas price averages tick up, multiple states have suspended or reduced their gas taxes, and President Donald Trump and his Cabinet have talked about doing the same. While a suspension would offer some relief, an NBC News analysis shows that gas prices would still average 14% more per gallon than they were at the start of the Iran war, even if all state and federal taxes were suspended. Average gas prices nationwide are up more than 30% since the war was launched at the end of February. Trump told reporters in May that he intended to suspend the 18 cents per gallon federal gas tax. Such a suspension would require an act of Congress. Democrats in the House and Senate proposed measures to suspend the gas tax in March. “All measures that can be taken to lower the price at the pump and lower the prices for Americans, this administration is in support of,” Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on NBC News’ “Meet the Press” in May. An average of 52 cents in taxes and fees is tacked onto every gallon of regular gas that’s pumped in America. Some of this revenue goes to the state levying the tax, and about 18 cents of it goes to the federal coffers. Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky and Utah have each made modifications to their gas tax since prices started climbing: Georgia’s gas tax was suspended from March to early June.Illinois put a six-month pause on a 7-cent gas tax increase scheduled to go into effect July 1.Indiana’s gas tax holiday was extended through to early August, then extended again to early September.Kentucky’s statewide gas tax reduction expired near the beginning of June.Utah reduced its gas tax from 37.9 cents to 31.9 cents, on regular gas only. How much these taxes and fees account for varies: 6.7% of Hawaii’s cost per gallon goes to taxes and fees, while 20.9% of the price people in Illinois pay comes from state and federal taxes and fees, according to an NBC News analysis. On average, across all states, 13.5% of the price paid per gallon goes to taxes and fees as of July. Taxes and fees range from 27 cents per gallon in Alaska to 89 cents per gallon in California. Note that local taxes are not factored into this data. Some of the federal gas tax money goes toward the Highway Trust Fund, which itself is used to fund highway and mass transit projects. One estimate put the cost of a gas tax holiday at a minimum of $2.5 billion per month. In March, Trump said at a Cabinet meeting that he had “thought about” suspending the federal gas tax. The federal gas tax has not been increased since Bill Clinton signed the last increase into law in 1993. The 18 cents it cost per gallon in 1993, after inflation, would be worth 8 cents in 2026 dollars. CORRECTION (May 14, 2026, 3:15 p.m. ET): A previous version of a chart and map in this article miscalculated Indiana’s and Utah’s average price per gallon of gas without state taxes. The state taxes had already been removed or reduced from the current price, which the graphics did not acknowledge.

articles.standfirst: IBGP será o responsável por organizar o certame para cargos de níveis fundamental, médio, técnico e superior. Próximo passo é a publicação do edital.
articles.summary: A banca IBGP organizará o concurso da Prefeitura de Porto Velho com 2.678 vagas para Saúde e Educação, abrangendo cargos de níveis fundamental a superior.
articles.body:
O novo concurso público da Prefeitura de Porto Velho terá organização do Instituto Brasileiro de Gestão e Pesquisa (IBGP). A seleção prevê 2.678 vagas para as secretarias municipais de Educação (Semed) e Saúde (Semusa), com oportunidades para candidatos de níveis fundamental, médio, técnico e superior. A contratação da banca foi oficializada por meio de dispensa de licitação publicada nesta quarta-feira (26).

Os valores das inscrições vão variar conforme o nível de escolaridade exigido para cada cargo, a dificuldade de organização do concurso e os critérios adotados em concursos anteriores. Segundo a tabela de referência do contrato, as taxas estimadas são:

Com a oficialização da banca, o próximo passo é a publicação do edital, que detalhará o cronograma das provas, número de vagas, conteúdo programático, valor das inscrições, entre outras informações.

O valor do contrato com o IBGP é de R$ 2,4 milhões. A empresa será responsável por todas as etapas do certame, desde o recebimento das inscrições até a homologação dos resultados finais.

No Portal da Transparência de Porto Velho, os candidatos podem consultar o termo de referência do concurso. O documento reúne informações como cargos, número de vagas, taxas de inscrição e estimativa de inscritos. Confira as oportunidades para diferentes níveis de escolaridade:

articles.title: Pneu de avião estoura durante pouso e afeta seis voos em MT | G1
articles.standfirst: Três voos com destino ao Aeroporto Internacional Marechal Rondon foram desviados para outros aeroportos e outros três tiveram atrasos nesta quinta-feira (27). Pista foi liberada após o procedimento de remoção.
articles.summary: Três voos com destino ao Aeroporto Internacional Marechal Rondon foram desviados para outros aeroportos e outros três tiveram atrasos nesta quinta-feira (27).
articles.body:
Aeroporto Internacional Marechal Rondon, em Várzea Grande — Foto: Reprodução

O rompimento de um dos pneus de um avião durante o pouso fechou temporariamente a pista do Aeroporto Internacional Marechal Rondon, em Várzea Grande , região metropolitana de Cuiabá, e afetou seis voos na manhã desta quinta-feira (27).

Segundo a Centro-Oeste Airports (COA), concessionária responsável pelo aeroporto, a ocorrência envolveu uma aeronave da aviação geral. O problema no pneu foi registrado durante o procedimento de pouso e provocou o bloqueio temporário da pista de pousos e decolagens.

Por causa da interdição, três voos que tinham o Aeroporto Marechal Rondon como destino precisaram ser desviados para outros aeroportos . Outros três voos que decolariam do terminal tiveram atrasos.

Após a ocorrência, a concessionária informou que acionou o Plano de Remoção de Aeronaves Interditadas (PRAI) para prestar suporte à aeronave e realizar a liberação da pista. De acordo com a COA, o procedimento de remoção foi concluído com segurança e as operações no aeroporto foram retomadas normalmente.

A concessionária orienta que passageiros com viagens previstas para esta quinta-feira entrem em contato diretamente com as companhias aéreas para consultar informações atualizadas sobre os voos.

articles.title: Onda de calor faz temperatura chegar a 34°C na capital e eleva risco de incêndios em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: O calor intenso e os baixos índices de umidade relativa do ar devem atingir praticamente todo o estado entre sexta-feira (28) e segunda-feira (31).
articles.summary: O calor intenso e os baixos índices de umidade relativa do ar devem atingir praticamente todo o estado entre sexta-feira (28) e segunda-feira (31).
articles.body:
Pedestres enfrentam sol forte e calor no Viaduto do Chá, na região central de São Paulo (07/03/2025) — Foto: CRIS FAGA/DRAGONFLY PRESS/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

A Defesa Civil do Estado de São Paulo alerta para uma onda de calor provocada pela atuação de uma massa de ar quente entre sexta-feira (28) e segunda-feira (31). Na capital, os termômetros podem chegar a 34°C no fim de semana, segundo o Climatempo.

O calor intenso e os baixos índices de umidade relativa do ar devem atingir praticamente todo o estado, com condições mais críticas previstas para as regiões norte e noroeste. No interior, a temperatura pode se aproximar dos 40°C.

A combinação de altas temperaturas, baixa umidade e tempo seco pode provocar forte sensação de calor, aumentar o desconforto térmico e intensificar o ressecamento do ambiente.

Essas condições também favorecem o ressecamento da vegetação, elevando significativamente o risco de queimadas e contribuindo para a rápida propagação de incêndios florestais, alerta a Defesa Civil

O Honda Prelude foi apresentado nesta quinta-feira (27) no Festival Interlagos 2026. As vendas começam hoje, por R$ 380 mil .

O cupê volta ao mercado brasileiro após 25 anos. Na década de 1990, o modelo teve Ayrton Senna como garoto-propaganda.

A sexta geração do Prelude tem um sistema híbrido que combina dois motores elétricos com um motor 2.0 a gasolina. O propulsor a combustão utiliza ciclo Atkinson e injeção direta, tecnologias que ajudam a reduzir o consumo de combustível. O conjunto entrega 203 cv de potência e 32,1 kgfm de torque.

O modelo também utiliza componentes do chassi do esportivo Civic Type R. Entre eles estão a suspensão independente nas quatro rodas, com sistema multilink na traseira e duplo eixo na dianteira, além de amortecedores adaptativos, que ajustam seu funcionamento de acordo com as condições de condução.

O Prelude será vendido em versão única. Entre os equipamentos estão rodas de 19 polegadas com pneus 235/40 R19, pedaleiras esportivas, painel digital de 10,2 polegadas e central multimídia de 9 polegadas com Google Assistente, Apple CarPlay e Android Auto.

O modelo também traz carregador de celular por indução, sistema de som Bose com oito alto-falantes, alerta de ponto cego e monitor de tráfego cruzado traseiro.

A carroceria tem configuração cupê 2+2 , com dois bancos dianteiros e dois lugares atrás. O banco traseiro é rebatível. Na frente, os bancos são esportivos, revestidos de couro claro e têm apoios de cabeça integrados e ajustes de posição.

Na prática, os bancos traseiros são mais adequados para trajetos curtíssimos e não oferecem conforto para quem tem mais de 1,80 m.

Honda Prelude no Autódromo de Interlagos — Foto: Divulgação / Honda

O Prelude vem equipado com o Honda SENSING, pacote de tecnologias que auxiliam o motorista durante a condução.

Frenagem automática para reduzir o risco ou a gravidade de colisões;

Correção de saída involuntária da pista;

Assistentes de permanência e centralização em faixa;

Controle de cruzeiro adaptativo , que ajusta a velocidade para manter distância do veículo à frente.

O carro também tem discos de freio dianteiros de 350 mm e pinças de quatro pistões Brembo. As pinças são pintadas de azul em referência ao sistema híbrido.

Produzido no Japão, o Prelude tem carroceria baixa e larga. O desenho inclui teto com duas elevações, para-lamas alargados e elementos aerodinâmicos na dianteira e na tampa do porta-malas.

O modelo será oferecido no Brasil nas cores Crystal Black Pearl , Rallye Red e Moonlit White Pearl .

Cabine do novo Honda Prelude — Foto: Divulgação / Honda

A garantia do veículo é de seis anos, sem limite de quilometragem. Para a bateria e os motores do sistema elétrico, a cobertura é de oito anos ou 160 mil quilômetros.

A pré-venda começa em 27 de agosto e segue até o fim de setembro. Os 50 compradores terão benefícios como capa de proteção, porcas antifurto, tapetes, condições especiais de pagamento e seguro, miniatura do Prelude, proteção para a pintura e experiências de direção promovidas pela Honda.

Propaganda do Honda Prelude no Japão em 1991 com Ayrton Senna — Foto: reprodução/redes sociais

Uma das principais novidades é o sistema S+ Shift . Acionado por um botão no console central, ele simula o funcionamento de um câmbio com trocas de marcha, embora o sistema híbrido não faça essas trocas da maneira convencional.

Para criar o efeito, o carro controla eletronicamente o funcionamento dos motores elétrico e a combustão.

O sistema também simula reduções de marcha e até o efeito do punta-tacco, técnica usada em carros esportivos para ajustar a rotação do motor durante uma redução. O S+ Shift funciona com os quatro modos de condução: Comfort, GT, Sport e Individual.

Os modos alteram características como a resposta do motor, o peso da direção, a rigidez dos amortecedores, o som reproduzido na cabine, as informações do painel e o funcionamento do controle de cruzeiro adaptativo.

O g1 testou o Honda Prelude no Autódromo de Interlagos, palco de algumas das principais conquistas de Ayrton Senna, que também foi garoto-propaganda do modelo.

O primeiro ponto é que o Prelude não tem a mesma proposta do Civic Type R. Com câmbio manual e foco maior no desempenho, o Type R foi desenvolvido para buscar tempos rápidos em autódromos. O Prelude tenta combinar esportividade com conforto para o uso cotidiano.

Nos primeiros quilômetros, com o modo Comfort selecionado, o Prelude mostrou uma condução confortável para duas pessoas. O sistema híbrido também tem como proposta reduzir o consumo de combustível.

Honda lança no Brasil o novo Prelude — Foto: Divulgação / Honda

O conjunto formado pelo motor 2.0 a combustão e pelo sistema híbrido é o mesmo utilizado no Honda Civic. O g1 já testou o modelo no Brasil e também mostrou por que ele desapareceu das lojas e das ruas.

Por dentro, a cabine segue o padrão de outros modelos da Honda. O quadro de instrumentos apresenta as informações de forma clara, com visual predominantemente em preto e branco. O couro claro com costuras azuis é um dos elementos que mais chamam atenção.

No modo Sport, o comportamento fica mais esportivo. O som do motor a combustão é reforçado artificialmente pelo sistema de áudio Bose, criando na cabine a sensação de um escapamento mais ruidoso.

Honda Prelude no Autódromo de Interlagos

A suspensão e a direção também funcionaram bem no circuito. Os componentes derivados do Civic Type R ajudam o Prelude a entrar e sair das curvas com facilidade e a manter a carroceria bem apoiada no asfalto.

Durante o teste, o conjunto de suspensão e chassi passou a impressão de que poderia lidar com mais potência sem comprometer o equilíbrio nas curvas.

Com a função S+ Shift, a experiência muda. O sistema cria artificialmente a sensação de trocas e reduções de marcha, mesmo em um conjunto híbrido no qual o motor elétrico tem papel central na movimentação do carro. O efeito lembra o funcionamento de um câmbio esportivo nas acelerações e retomadas.

Na pista, a simulação é convincente. As mudanças no som e na resposta do carro dão a sensação de que um câmbio está realizando trocas de marcha, embora o funcionamento real do sistema seja diferente.

A conclusão é que o Prelude pode encontrar seu público no Brasil. E a Honda poderá ampliar a oferta dependendo da procura pelo modelo.

Entre os potenciais compradores estão consumidores atraídos pelo visual e pela história do Prelude, especialmente aqueles que acompanharam o modelo nas décadas de 1980 e 1990.

Cerca de 25 anos depois, esse público volta a ter a opção de comprar um Prelude no Brasil, agora com uma proposta que combina esportividade e conforto para o uso cotidiano.

Suspensão traseira: independente multilink;

Tipo de híbrido: convencional, sem recarga externa;

Potência do motor a combustão: 143 cv a 6.000 rpm;

Torque do motor a combustão: 19,1 kgfm a 4.500 rpm;

articles.title: Gestão Trump negocia com governo interino da Venezuela para assumir parte das reservas de petróleo do país, diz site | G1
articles.standfirst: País sul-americano possui as maiores reservas conhecidas de petróleo do mundo. Delcy Rodríguez atua como presidente interina desde o sequestro de Maduro por Washington, mas Marco Rubio, secretário de Estado dos EUA, é apontado como quem dita as ordens para Caracas.
articles.summary: País sul-americano possui as maiores reservas conhecidas de petróleo do mundo. Delcy Rodríguez atua como presidente interina desde o sequestro de Maduro por Washington, mas Marco Rubio, secretário de Estado dos EUA, é apontado como quem dita as ordens para Caracas.
articles.body:
Tanques com o logo da PDVSA em refinaria em Curaçao — Foto: Andres Martinez Casares/Reuters

A gestão Trump está conversando com o governo interino da Venezuela para assumir uma participação acionária nas enormes reservas de petróleo do país, segundo o site americano Axios.

O site diz ter ouvido dois altos funcionários da Casa Branca.

A Venezuela possui as maiores reservas conhecidas de petróleo do mundo. Em 3 de janeiro, uma operação militar americana realizou uma invasão ao país, sequestrando o presidente Nicolás Maduro.

Maduro foi levado a Nova York, onde se encontra preso aguardando julgamento.

Em seu lugar, foi nomeada como presidente interina Delcy Rodríguez, vice de Maduro, mas cujo governo tem tomado medidas pró-Washington, como a soltura de dissidentes políticos e o envio de petróleo para os EUA .

Marco Rubio durante evento em Washington em 4 de agosto de 2026. — Foto: Kevin Lamarque/Reuters

O secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, é apontado como a autoridade que dita de fato as ordens em Caracas .

O republicano tem defendido uma aproximação com Caracas principalmente por causa da importância do país no mercado de petróleo. O tema ganhou ainda mais relevância para a Casa Branca após a escalada do conflito com o Irã, que pressionou os preços internacionais da commodity.

Ao mesmo tempo, a oposição venezuelana e entidades de defesa dos direitos humanos têm pedido um avanço mais rápido das negociações políticas. A cobrança também encontra apoio entre parlamentares democratas e republicanos no Congresso dos Estados Unidos .

Rubio já havia defendido que a Venezuela passaria por três etapas após a saída de Maduro: estabilização econômica, reorganização política e uma transição para eleições.

articles.title: Litros de água jorram para o alto na rua após rompimento de adutora  | G1
articles.standfirst: Situação ocorreu nesta quinta-feira (27) no bairro Forquilhas, em São José. Casan declarou que abastecimento foi prejudicado na região.
articles.summary: Situação ocorreu nesta quinta-feira (27) no bairro Forquilhas, em São José.
articles.body:
Litros de água jorraram para o alto em uma rua de São José , na Grande Florianópolis , após o rompimento de uma adutora na tarde desta quinta-feira (27) (assista acima).

Uma equipe da Companhia Catarinense de Águas e Saneamento (Casan) está no local, no bairro Forquilhas, para fazer o conserto.

A companhia informou que o abastecimento foi prejudicado nos bairros Forquilhas, Potecas, Colônia Santana, Sertão do Imaruim e Área industrial . Contudo, a Casan declarou que imóveis com caixa d'água não devem sentir os efeitos do problema .

A previsão é de que a normalização do abastecimento ocorra gradativamente ao longo da madrugada desta sexta-feira (28). A previsão é de que a obra seja concluída e a via liberada para o tráfego no final da tarde de sexta.

Água jorra na rua após rompimento de adutora em São José, na Grande Florianópolis — Foto: Montagem/Reprodução/André Lux/NSC TV

Obra de empresa terceirizada rompeu adutora

O rompimento ocorreu às 14h40 na Rua Antônio Jovita Duarte, informou a prefeitura. Foi na rua, próximo ao calçamento onde acontece uma obra de uma empresa terceirizada da Secretaria Municipal de Infraestrutura.

A intervenção era feita para a solução de uma infiltração de água no local e acabou atingindo a tubulação da adutora. Diante da situação, a Casan foi chamada.

A prefeitura informou que a Guarda Municipal estava no local na tarde desta quinta para orientar o trânsito. Além do reparo da adutora, a Casan também realizou a limpeza da via.

A Rua Antônio Jovita Duarte permanecia sinalizada e parcialmente interditada na tarde desta quinta para garantir a segurança das equipes que trabalham no local.

Após a conclusão dos serviços, a Secretaria de Infraestrutura também fará o reparo da pavimentação no trecho atingido.

articles.title: Trump diz que Putin não vai atacar o território da Otan e minimiza viagem do diretor da CIA a Moscou | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo reportagem do "Wall Street Journal", diretor da CIA viajou a Moscou para pedir à Rússia que não realize ofensivas contra países da aliança militar.
articles.summary: Segundo reportagem do "Wall Street Journal", diretor da CIA viajou a Moscou para pedir à Rússia que não realize ofensivas contra países da aliança militar.
articles.body:
Trump fala com a imprensa na Casa Branca após assinar ordem executiva renomeando o Lago Ontário como Lago América — Foto: Evan Vucci/Reuters

O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmou nesta quinta-feira (27) que o presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, não vai atacar o território da Otan (Organização do Tratado do Atlântico Norte). A declaração ocorre dias após a viagem surpresa do diretor da CIA a Moscou .

Mais cedo nesta quinta, Trump disse ao site norte-americano Axios que o chefe da CIA, John Ratcliffe, não havia sido enviado a Moscou para entregar uma mensagem em particular.

"Ratcliffe se reúne com seu homólogo russo uma vez a cada seis meses ou uma vez por ano. Eles têm um relacionamento muito bom. Não houve mensagem alguma e não houve nada de incomum", afirmou Trump.

Segundo uma reportagem do jornal The Wall Street Journal, publicada na quarta (26), Ratcliffe viajou a Moscou para pedir à Rússia que não ataque nenhum país da Otan .

De acordo com pessoas informadas sobre a viagem ouvidas pelo jornal, Ratcliffe disse para as autoridades russas que Moscou não deve tentar testar a capacidade de reação da aliança militar com uma ofensiva limitada contra um dos membros da Otan.

A viagem surpresa foi confirmada pelo Kremlin. O porta-voz da presidência russa, Dmitry Peskov, afirmou que Ratcliffe se reuniu com representantes da inteligência do país, mas não com Vladimir Putin. Segundo ele, o presidente foi informado sobre os contatos.

O alerta dos Estados Unidos foi motivado por novas avaliações de inteligência que apontam para a possibilidade de Putin tentar medir, nos próximos anos, até que ponto os países da Otan estariam dispostos a reagir a uma agressão russa, segundo o WSJ.

O jornal informou que os cenários avaliados como possíveis pelos norte-americanos vão desde ataques cibernéticos até uma incursão terrestre de pequena escala contra um dos integrantes da aliança.

Os riscos surgiram em meio à guerra na Ucrânia e à baixa dos estoques de determinadas munições dos países ocidentais, incluindo os EUA. Segundo o WSJ, essas informações poderiam influenciar Putin a tomar uma decisão sobre o assunto.

articles.title: Violência contra a mulher: projeto em Juruti promove autonomia | G1
articles.standfirst: Iniciativa no oeste do Pará ganha força em meio a alerta nacional: a violência psicológica lidera as denúncias no Ligue 180 em 2026.
articles.summary: O projeto Move +Mulheres capacita empreendedoras em Juruti para combater a violência contra a mulher e a dependência financeira no oeste do Pará.
articles.body:
Como romper o ciclo de abusos e silenciamento que afeta milhares de mulheres todos os dias? Em Juruti , no oeste do Pará, a resposta tem sido construída por meio do conhecimento. Um grupo de 40 mulheres do município está participando de uma capacitação voltada ao empreendedorismo, com o objetivo de fortalecer seus negócios e ampliar sua independência financeira.

A iniciativa ganha ainda mais relevância diante de um cenário de alerta: a violência psicológica foi o tipo de agressão contra a mulher mais denunciado ao Ligue 180 entre janeiro e julho de 2026. Das 98.705 denúncias registradas no período no país, 35,2% (35.284 casos) envolviam esse tipo de abuso, segundo o Ministério das Mulheres.

Em Juruti, a discussão sobre a segurança das mulheres tornou-se ainda mais urgente após um caso de extrema violência em julho deste ano, quando um vigilante invadiu a casa da ex-companheira, matou o atual marido dela, baleou a mulher e a filha, e morreu em seguida. O episódio chocou a região e acendeu o debate sobre prevenção.

O perigo invisível da violência psicológica

Embora a violência psicológica nem sempre termine em tragédia física, especialistas alertam que o abuso se estabelece de forma silenciosa e gradual, sendo frequentemente naturalizado pelas vítimas.

"A violência não começa no grito. Muitas vezes começa no silêncio, na desvalorização constante e na perda gradual de autonomia emocional e material", explica Karen Scavacini, psicóloga e fundadora do Instituto Vita Alere.

A falta de uma rede de apoio e a dependência financeira são apontadas como os principais obstáculos para que as mulheres consigam sair de relacionamentos abusivos.

De acordo com Scavacini, a autonomia financeira não anula os mecanismos de proteção do Estado, mas funciona como uma ferramenta crucial para ampliar as possibilidades de escolha da mulher.

'Parei de trabalhar só com intuição': a história de Vanessa

É nesse contexto de fortalecimento que atua o programa Move +Mulheres, realizado em Juruti pelo Grupo +Unidos. A iniciativa oferece cursos, workshops e mentorias de negócios para empreendedoras locais.

Uma das participantes é Vanessa Santarém da Silva, de 31 anos. Enfermeira de formação e mãe, ela recorreu ao empreendedorismo em 2021, após ficar desempregada e precisar de uma fonte de renda para sustentar a filha. Foi assim que nasceu a loja Tulipa Kids.

"Eu precisava recomeçar. Empreender foi a forma que encontrei de sustentar minha família e ajudar outras mulheres a fazer o mesmo", conta Vanessa.

Após passar pelo programa de capacitação, Vanessa aprendeu a traçar estratégias de marketing digital e planejamento financeiro. "Parei de trabalhar só com intuição e passei a empreender com técnica, planejamento e metas reais", celebra.

Os dados do Ligue 180 mostram que a violência psicológica ultrapassou fisicamente outras formas de agressão nas estatísticas de 2026. Esse tipo de abuso é caracterizado por:

Manipulação e isolamento social (proibir de ver amigos e familiares);

Controle sobre roupas, comportamento, trabalho e dinheiro.

O debate sobre o tema ganha força durante a campanha Agosto Lilás, que em 2026 marca os 20 anos da Lei Maria da Penha, principal ferramenta jurídica de proteção à mulher no Brasil.

Se você ou alguém que você conhece está passando por uma situação de violência (física, psicológica, patrimonial ou sexual), denuncie:

Ligue 180: Central de Atendimento à Mulher (gratuito, sigiloso e funciona 24 horas por dia).

Polícia Militar (190): Indicado para situações de emergência e flagrante.

articles.title: Avalanche de lama no Nepal e Tibete: veja vídeo de fuga desesperada | G1
articles.standfirst: Homem estava filmando calmamente até perceber que o perigo era maior do que ele pensava e começar a correr junto com os colegas para o alto da montanha.
articles.summary: O registro de um funcionário de hidrelétrica mostra a fuga desesperada de uma avalanche de lama no Nepal que já deixou centenas de mortos e desaparecidos.
articles.body:
O funcionário de uma usina hidrelétrica atingida pela avalanche de lama que destruiu vários locais na fronteira do Nepal com o Tibete na quarta-feira (26) postou vídeos de tudo que viveu ao lado dos colegas durante o desastre.

Nas imagens impressionantes, Vivek Shrestha aparece inicialmente calmo, filmando enquanto a inundação se aproxima. No entanto, ao perceber que a força d'água era grande demais e que ele estava em risco, começa a correr e escalar para subir mais na montanha.

Funcionários de hidrelétrica correndo para fugir de avalanche no Nepal — Foto: Vivek Shrestha / Instagram / Reprodução

O vídeo, que mostra todo o desespero dos funcionários, viralizou e foi visto por mais de 36,6 milhões de pessoas. Na legenda, Vivek escreveu:

"Hoje houve uma enchente em Mailung, em Rasuwa, e estou em estado grave. Fui resgatado de helicóptero".

O funcionário da hidrelétrica nepalesa ainda postou mais dois vídeos. No segundo, já em segurança, ele filmou a força da água que descia o rio em grande volume.

No terceiro, depois que a situação se acalmou, ele e os colegas aparecem sentados à beira do rio, que estava quase sem água e cheio de lama em seu leito, à espera do resgate.

O número de mortos na avalanche de lama passou de 300 na manhã desta quinta-feira (27), segundo as autoridades .

Cerca de 1.500 pessoas seguem desaparecidas, e as equipes de resgate continuam as buscas em meio à lama e os escombros.

➡️ COMO É A REGIÃO? A área afetada é uma região de fronteira com apelo turístico e cercada por uma das cadeias de montanhas mais famosas do mundo, a Cordilheira do Himalaia.

Embora não seja muito populosa, a região conecta diversas cidades e vilas e abriga usinas hidrelétricas e um porto, além de um posto fronteiriço entre o Nepal e a China — que controla o território do Tibete. O posto é uma das principais portas de entrada e saída para quem viaja entre os dois países.

A avalanche atingiu Syabrubesi, ponto de partida da famosa trilha do Langtang, e outras áreas frequentadas por viajantes que fazem o passeio de peregrinação hindu ao Kailash Mansarovar.

Outros vídeos da região, que sugiram ao longo desta quarta, também mostram cenas assustadoras : a destruição do porto de Gyirong (veja acima) , o desespero de passageiros de um ônibus em uma das vilas do Nepal atingidas e mais.

Fuga de funcionários de hidrelétrica do Nepal durante avalanche — Foto: Vivek Shrestha / Instagram / Reprodução

articles.title: Palmas tem desempenho histórico em ranking de competitividade  | G1
articles.standfirst: Palmas se tornou o primeiro município das regiões Norte e Nordeste a ficar entre os 15 mais competitivos do país desde o início do levantamento.
articles.summary: Palmas se tornou o primeiro município das regiões Norte e Nordeste a ficar entre os 15 mais competitivos do país desde o início do levantamento.
articles.body:
Vista aérea da região central de Palmas — Foto: Regiane Rocha/Prefeitura de Palmas

Palmas registrou um resultado histórico na edição de 2026 do Ranking de Competitividade dos Municípios. Elaborado pelo Centro de Liderança Pública (CLP) em parceria com a Gove Digital, o estudo colocou a capital tocantinense na 13ª posição entre os municípios mais competitivos do país.

Com o resultado, Palmas se tornou o primeiro município das regiões Norte e Nordeste a ficar entre os 15 mais competitivos do país desde o início do levantamento.

Até então, o melhor resultado entre os municípios do Norte e Nordeste era de Recife (PE), que ficou em 37º lugar no ranking nacional em 2023.

Vitória (ES) ficou em primeiro lugar no ranking pela primeira vez. O top 10 também é formado por Florianópolis (SC), Porto Alegre (RS), Curitiba (PR), São Paulo (SP), São Caetano do Sul (SP), Maringá (PR), Campinas (SP), Jaraguá do Sul (SC) e Barueri (SP).

O desempenho de Palmas acompanha uma série de avanços registrados em municípios do Norte e Nordeste.

Segundo a pesquisa, Palmas ocupa a 4ª colocação nacional em Inserção Econômica, a 5ª em Economia, a 6ª em Inovação e Dinamismo Econômico e a 119ª em Saneamento. A capital é o município mais bem colocado da Região Norte nesses indicadores.

No Tocantins, Gurupi também se destacou. O município ocupa a 122ª colocação nacional em Sociedade e a 134ª em Qualidade da Educação. Além disso, avançou 128 posições no pilar Saneamento, um dos maiores ganhos da Região Norte.

Araguaína avançou 147 posições no indicador de Telecomunicações, ficando entre os maiores avanços do país.

Em sua sétima edição, o Ranking de Competitividade dos Municípios avalia 423 cidades brasileiras com mais de 80 mil habitantes. O estudo reúne 65 indicadores, distribuídos em 13 pilares relacionados à gestão pública:

A organização tem 18 anos de existência e defende um Estado Democrático de Direito eficiente no uso dos recursos públicos e baseado em princípios republicanos.

articles.title: Louisiana announces $20,000 reward after bald eagle is fatally shot near Lake Peigneur, investigators seek person responsible for killing protected bird
articles.summary: US News: The reward for information leading to a conviction in the fatal shooting of a bald eagle in southern Louisiana has risen to $20,000, as state and fede.
articles.body: The reward for information leading to a conviction in the fatal shooting of a bald eagle in southern Louisiana has risen to $20,000, as state and federal wildlife investigators continue searching for whoever killed the protected bird. The eagle was discovered injured on December 5, 2025, near the intersection of Robert Road and Wilmer Road in rural Vermilion Parish, close to Lake Peigneur. Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries (LDWF) agents located and captured the bird before it could be examined, but officials determined that its injuries were consistent with a fatal gunshot wound. The eagle died shortly after being found and was later sent to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service for a detailed necropsy. The case has remained unresolved despite investigators receiving several tips. The Centre for Biological Diversity, which increased its contribution to the reward, is now urging anyone with information to come forward.Why has the bald eagle killing triggered a $20,000 reward?The reward has grown substantially as investigators attempt to generate fresh leads and identify the person responsible for killing the bald eagle in Vermilion Parish, Louisiana. According to the Centre for Biological Diversity’s August 24 press release, the organisation increased its contribution to the overall reward, bringing the total to as much as $20,000 for information that leads to a conviction. The fund now includes $13,000 from the Centre for Biological Diversity, $3,500 from Humane World for Animals, $2,500 from the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and up to $1,000 from Louisiana Operation Game Thief. The Center’s latest contribution follows an earlier increase in February, when it helped raise the reward to $15,000. With the case still unresolved and investigators continuing to seek information, the larger financial incentive is intended to encourage witnesses or anyone with relevant knowledge to come forward. The Centre for Biological Diversity said the increased reward could help provide the crucial lead needed to bring the case to a conclusion.How was the Louisiana bald eagle killed?The investigation began after LDWF agents were alerted to an injured bald eagle in Vermilion Parish on December 5, 2025. Personnel found the bird near Robert Road and Wilmer Road, captured it and transported it for examination. Officials determined that the eagle had suffered a fatal injury consistent with a gunshot wound, and it died soon after discovery. The remains were subsequently sent to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service for a more extensive necropsy. Months later, investigators have yet to identify a suspect publicly. The LDWF and U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service have continued working on the case and have received numerous tips. Still, authorities are seeking additional information that could help establish who was responsible for the shooting.What laws protect bald eagles in the US?The shooting is being investigated as a federal wildlife offence because bald eagles are protected under the Bald and Golden Eagle Protection Act. According to wildlife officials, illegally killing a bald eagle can result in a fine of up to $5,000 and as much as one year in prison, while a civil restitution fine of up to another $5,000 may also apply. The species has particular significance in the United States because the bald eagle has served as the country’s national symbol since Congress adopted it in 1782. The bird also represents one of the country's major wildlife conservation successes. After populations declined because of habitat loss, hunting and the widespread use of DDT, conservation measures helped the species recover, eventually leading to its removal from the federal endangered species list in 2007.How can people report information about the Louisiana eagle killing?Wildlife officials are asking anyone who may have information about the shooting to contact Louisiana Operation Game Thief. Tips can be submitted through the hotline at 1-800-442-2511 or through the Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries’ tip411 programme. People can text LADWF followed by their tip to 847411, while information can also be submitted through the free LADWF Tips mobile application. The hotline and tip411 system are monitored around the clock, and authorities say people providing information can request anonymity. Investigators are particularly interested in additional information that could help establish what happened to the eagle and identify the person responsible. The Centre for Biological Diversity, which announced the increased reward on August 24, said it hopes the larger incentive will encourage someone with relevant knowledge to come forward.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Is Iran war diplomacy ramping up, as Qatar, Oman, Pakistan officials visit?
articles.summary: There are signs both sides could be ready to de-escalate, at least militarily, analysts say.
articles.body:
Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani is visiting Tehran on Thursday for talks about de-escalating tensions and reviving failed negotiations between Iran and the United States.

His visit comes amid a flurry of high-level delegations travelling to Tehran in recent days, with mediators rallying to persuade the warring sides back to the negotiating table despite continued hardline posturing on both sides.

Sheikh Mohammed, who is also Qatar’s foreign minister, will meet with “a number of Iranian officials” in Tehran to discuss ending hostilities and to “create the conditions conducive to dialogue”, a spokesperson said.

He will also address the issue of the critical Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf, and “the need for it to return to the status quo before February 28”. The narrow waterway has been mostly closed to shipping since early March, when Iran closed it, and shipping traffic, which carried more than one-fifth of global oil and gas supplies before the war, has collapsed , sending global energy markets into crisis.

Qatar is a key behind-the-scenes negotiator between Washington and Tehran and was pivotal in securing a memorandum of understanding (MoU) in June that briefly paused hostilities, but the deal has since expired.

Here’s what else we know about the renewed push for talks:

On Monday, Pakistan’s army chief Asim Munir met with several high-ranking officials in Tehran, including Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran’s chief negotiator.

He also met with General Mohsen Rezaei, the recently appointed secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council.

On Tuesday, Oman’s Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi met his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi in Tehran to discuss the Strait of Hormuz, which has become the biggest flashpoint in the conflict. The two countries have been negotiating how to jointly govern the shared passageway for weeks.

Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi on the same day announced the two sides had agreed to a new temporary shipping route in the strait that would see vessels enter through Iranian waters, and give Tehran partial control over exit routes. However, Iran emphasised that the strait will not reopen until the US lifts sanctions and unfreezes Iran’s assets.

Officially, the US and Iran are still at war and have each declared the other side as defeated, despite both suffering economically and politically from it.

Amid US news reports that the US may be running low on vital interceptor missiles and equipment in the Middle East, the Trump administration has shifted to a strategy of economic pressure on Iran, announcing new sanctions this week and threatening other countries which continue to do business with it with secondary sanctions .

A major obstacle is the closed Strait of Hormuz. Iran wants to continue controlling the waterway, which flows through the territorial waters of Iran and Oman, as it has done in the course of the conflict, but Washington opposes this stance and wants to return to the pre-war arrangement under which all shipping passed freely through the strait.

While Trump declared this week that all seamines had been removed from the strait, experts warn that some may have been missed, meaning this remains an additional risk to ships.

The US, meanwhile, is also continuing its naval blockade on Iranian ports in and around the strait, hampering Iranian oil exports .

Possibly. The breakthrough in talks between Iran and Oman over the Strait of Hormuz has been viewed by some experts as a sign that Tehran is open to negotiations.

The US will also begin returning diplomatic staff who were earlier evacuated from their Middle East stations as early as next week, according to the Reuters news agency on Thursday.

US staff and their family members were withdrawn after the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran in late February.

Staff were evacuated from Jordan, Bahrain, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Lebanon and Iraq, after the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran, and as Tehran retaliated on neighbouring countries.

US embassies in Saudi Arabia and Kuwait were temporarily shut down after coming under fire.

Now, posts in Jordan, Israel and Oman will be fully restored, US media reported.

In the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Lebanon, missions will be capped at 85 percent, while posts in Iraq, Kuwait and Bahrain will be limited to 75 percent.

It has not been confirmed whether the US decision to return embassy staff is connected with the ongoing diplomatic push. However, analysts say it demonstrates Washington’s confidence that the war will not escalate militarily, despite the breakdown of face-to-face talks.

What have the US and Iran said about peace talks?

Statements from both sides stand in stark contrast to the new push for peace, however.

US President Donald Trump told Al Jazeera on Wednesday he is in “no hurry” to resume talks with Iran and said he believes economic and military action against Tehran will both be effective.

Washington has notably shifted away from military operations to a strategy of increased economic pressure on Tehran, however. On Monday, a sweeping set of sanctions was unleashed on Iranian firms and Tehran’s trade partners .

More than 60 individuals and organisations were targeted across five sectors that Washington accuses of sustaining Iran’s economy: digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping. Oil and financial sectors have been under sanctions for some time.

The new sanctions affect entities in China, Hong Kong, the UK, Ukraine, Syria, France, Malaysia, Singapore and several other countries.

Iran, meanwhile, has rejected and condemned the new sanctions. In a letter to the United Nations on Wednesday, Iran’s Foreign Minister Araghchi described the US sanctions as an “act of state and economic terrorism”. He urged member states not to implement them.

High-ranking military officials recently appointed in a security cabinet shuffle have also continued to issue defiant statements. When Pakistan’s Munir visited, Supreme National Security Council secretary Rezaei reportedly told him that Iran “distrusts America”.

However, Iranian President Pezeshkian has sounded a slightly different tune.

Last week, he called for Iran to negotiate from a place of strength, not weakness, saying: “It is better that we bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power and dignity.”

The Iranian president’s authority is, however, limited, as he is subordinate to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei . Hardliners, especially in the military, have accused his government of conceding to the US by agreeing to the June MoU, although the president has pushed back against that criticism, saying the agreement did not represent capitulation.

What does the renewed diplomatic activity mean?

There’s no confirmation yet that the US is directly involved in the flurry of diplomatic activity seen this past week.

However, some analysts speculate that the US’s increased economic pressure on Iran could be a means to force Tehran to agree to negotiations.

Ali Vaez, of the International Crisis Group think tank, said Washington is looking to initiate a “financial apocalypse” in Iran by using the military blockade alongside sanctions on Iran’s already battered economy .

“The Islamic Republic has faced all of these before, though rarely in tandem and at a time when its challenges are already so acute,” Vaez said in a statement to journalists.

“The question is whether this new chapter in economic brinksmanship is intended to be a zero-sum campaign aimed at collapsing the regime, or leverage towards an agreement.”

articles.title: Trial for 9/11 accused, including Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, set for June 2028
articles.summary: After two decades at Guantánamo Bay, trials for four alleged 9/11 conspirators have been set for 2028.
articles.body:
A US military judge has ordered Khalid Sheikh Mohammed , the alleged mastermind of the September 11 attacks, and three co-defendants to stand trial, more than two decades after their arrest.

Air Force Lieutenant Colonel Michael Schrama issued the scheduling order on Wednesday, setting opening proceedings for June 5, 2028.

The ruling comes after a US appeals court blocked plea deals that would have let Mohammed and two co-defendants avoid the death penalty.

The case has been stalled for years by disputes over evidence obtained while the men were held in CIA prisons and subjected to torture.

Schrama turned down a prosecution bid to open the trial in early 2027, arguing that timeline wouldn’t leave enough room to work through the disputes.

“A realistic trial date must account for the hearing and resolution of pretrial evidentiary and compliance motions,” he wrote.

Mohammed faces trial along with Walid bin Attash, Mustafa al-Hawsawi and Ali Abdul Aziz Ali.

Under the order, a jury of military service members will first be selected, with opening statements to follow 30 days later. The defence is due to begin presenting its case 60 days after prosecutors finish theirs and the trial will close with a sentencing phase.

Mohammed and two of his co-defendants struck a deal in 2024 that would have spared them the possibility of the death penalty in exchange for a guilty plea.

Then-Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin revoked that deal within days and an appeals court backed his move last month.

Mohammed was regarded as one of al-Qaeda chief Osama bin Laden’s key lieutenants until he was captured by US forces in Pakistan in March 2003. He spent three years in secret CIA prisons before arriving in Guantanamo in 2006.

articles.title: Lindsay Clancy trial live updates: Closing arguments end, jury deliberates murder vs. manslaughter
articles.summary: Closing arguments ended today in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy, who killed her three young children — Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months — at their home before attempting to kill herself on January 2023.
articles.body:
What to know about the trial Closing arguments ended today in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy, who killed her three young children — Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months — at their home before she tried to kill herself in January 2023. Jurors are now deliberating over charges of first-degree murder — involving “deliberate premeditation and extreme atrocity” — with the option to consider lesser manslaughter charges. No verdict was reached today and jurors will resume deliberations tomorrow morning. Clancy’s mental health is a key issue. Her defense, led by attorney Kevin Reddington, argued she was experiencing postpartum psychosis and was compelled to act by a hallucinated voice when she strangled her children. The prosecution’s closing argument, delivered by Assistant District Attorney Jennifer Sprague, said Clancy was a "functioning mom" who knew "right and wrong." Clancy put a level of planning into the killings that indicates she was not psychotic, Sprague argued. The five-week trial has taken over podcasts, social media and conversations beyond the Massachusetts courtroom. Clancy, 36, has also emerged as a symbol of the gaps in maternal healthcare.

articles.title: ‘Worst 24 hours of my life’: Indo-American doctor appeals for help after parents go missing in Nepal floods
articles.summary: US News: An Indo-American doctor pleads for information about her missing parents after they disappeared during devastating floods near the Nepal-China border while on pilgrimage to Mount Kailash. Hundreds remain unaccounted for following the disaster, with a rising death toll in Nepal and Tibet.
articles.body: An Indo-American doctor has made an urgent appeal for information about her parents after the couple went missing during catastrophic flash floods and landslides near the Nepal-China border while travelling on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash.Radhika Sharma said her parents, Ramesh Sharma, 65, and Neelam Sharma, 64, have been “missing and unaccounted” for since they crossed the Nepal-China border at around 8am local time on Wednesday, about 40 minutes before the floods struck. She said she has not heard from them since.“It’s been probably over 24 hours, and probably been the worst 24 hours of my life, my brother’s life,” Sharma told NBC. “We’re just waiting to hear from them, and just any information, honestly.”Sharma turned to social media for help and appealed to anyone with contacts in Nepal and Tibet who might have information about her parents. In a post on X, she asked people with direct contacts in Gyirong and Tibet, local hospitals, rescue operations, government authorities or local media to contact her immediately.“I would greatly appreciate any help. Any contacts, any information,” she wrote.The couple were travelling as part of a pilgrimage to sacred Mount Kailash when the floods and landslides struck the Himalayan border region. Their disappearance comes as authorities continue searching for hundreds of people who remain unaccounted for following the disaster.The floods have killed at least 165 people in Nepal, according to figures provided by Nepalese authorities. Three deaths have also been reported in Tibet, where 558 people are missing.The figures have continued to change as authorities work to establish the full scale of the disaster. A later update put the death toll in Nepal at 270, while 826 are still missing. Nepalese officials said dozens of bridges had been destroyed and nearly 40 kilometres (25 miles) of roads damaged, making it harder for rescue teams to reach affected areas.The Nepalese Army has been using helicopters to reach people stranded by the floods. Army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet said more than 100 people had been rescued from flood-hit areas on Thursday morning, while at least eight foreign nationals were airlifted to Kathmandu. Army teams also evacuated people trapped inside facilities connected to the Trishuli hydropower project.The disaster has also affected Indian pilgrims travelling to Mount Kailash. An official spokesperson for India's Ministry of External Affairs said 21 Indian nationals from Tamil Nadu who had travelled for the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra had been rescued in Nepal.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Two airport workers in Germany die after contracting malaria
articles.summary: Two workers at Germany’s Frankfurt Airport have died after contracting malaria believed to have been spread by a mosquito brought into the country via an aircraft.
articles.body: Two workers at Germany’s Frankfurt Airport have died after contracting malaria believed to have been spread by a mosquito brought into the country via an aircraft. A total of six employees became infected with what is known as airport malaria, Fraport, the company that operates the airport, told CNN. Two subsequently died. “We are shocked and deeply saddened by the loss of our colleagues, and our thoughts are with their families and friends,” Fraport said. The four other employees have since recovered, according to a report in German news magazine Der Spiegel. Airport malaria is a very rare form of the disease’s transmission and occurs when a mosquito survives a flight from a malaria-endemic country and transmits the disease at or near the airport. In mid-July, the Robert Koch Institute (RKI), Germany’s national public health institute, noted that there had been an outbreak of malaria cases among employees at the airport, with multiple individuals falling ill between July 4 and July 6. It is believed the disease was spread by an Anopheles mosquito brought into Germany on an aircraft, the RKI noted. Frankfurt health authorities are investigating the incident. Among German nationals, malaria almost exclusively affects long-distance travelers who contract the disease from an infected mosquito in an area where it is prevalent, the RKI said, adding that infection at an airport was rare and can lead to a delay in diagnosis due to health professionals rarely suspecting malaria initially. Early diagnosis and treatment of malaria are crucial to preventing severe illness and fatalities, it added. Fraport said it had since advised employees to inform their doctor that they work at Frankfurt Airport and that cases of airport malaria had been reported, “to help ensure they receive appropriate medical examination and treatment.” Mosquito traps have now been installed at the airport, Fraport said, adding that the mosquitos captured will be genetically analyzed by the Institute of Tropical Medicine in Antwerp, Belgium, to determine their species and origin. The last case of a malaria infection at an airport in Germany occurred in 2023, also at Frankfurt Airport, according to RKI. Frankfurt Airport is considered Germany’s busiest in terms of the volume of passengers. It is also the primary hub for the country’s flagship Lufthansa carrier.

articles.title: Thieves steal Bronze Age artifacts from Spanish museum in four-minute heist
articles.summary: The Treasure of Villena is a unique trove of almost ten kilos of gold, bowls, bottles and bracelets dating back to the Bronze Age.
articles.body:
Thieves have stolen jewellery and artefacts from one of the most important prehistoric gold collections at a museum in the Spanish province of Alicante.

The Treasure of Villena is a unique trove of almost ten kilos of gold, bowls, bottles and bracelets dating back to the Bronze Age.

Police are still assessing exactly how many items were stolen in the raid, which took place in the early hours of Thursday morning. The museum confirmed to the BBC that rings, bowls and bracelets were among the items seized.

It is the latest high profile heist on a European museum. Last year, thieves staged a brazen robbery at the Louvre in Paris in broad daylight.

The operation at Villena Museum was "super fast and super professional", a spokesman for Villena town council said.

The city council said the robbery began with a diversion. Around 05:15 local time (03:15 GMT), the alarms went off at the local sports centre, sending police there first, Spanish media reported.

The museum's alarm then went off around 05:20. It took the thieves just four minutes to sweep through museum and leave the building before officers arrived.

The Mayor of Villena, Fulgencio Cerdán, said the thieves "stole a large part of the treasure," specifically all the gold, El Pais reported.

The museum's collection, which dates back to around 1,000 BC, is mainly gold items, but there are also pieces of silver, iron and amber.

It consists of more than 60 bronze age objects, including 29 bracelets, 11 bowls, three bottles and other miscellaneous pieces.

The town is "devastated," Cerdán said. "They've taken most of the treasure."

"I'm even trembling. The truth is that for those of us from Villena, this destroys us. It's part of our heritage, of our wealth," the mayor said.

The collection was discovered in 1963 by archaeologist Jose María Soler in a vessel sunk in a dried-out riverbed in Villena.

The Villena council spokesman insisted there had been "no failure" by the museum.

The past year has seen a series of raids on European museums. In October 2025, thieves broke into the Louvre museum in Paris in broad daylight, stealing jewellery worth $102m (£75m) before escaping on scooters, in a heist that took about eight minutes.

Last week, four works "of extraordinary value" by Renaissance artist Antonello da Messina were stolen from a museum in Sicily, Italy's culture ministry said.

Earlier this month, Italian police said they had recovered paintings by Renoir, Cezanne and Matisse worth over $10.4m (£7.6m) which were stolen from the Magnani-Rocca Foundation museum near Parma.

articles.title: In 1904, a 1,227-foot Cincinnati railroad warehouse was among the world’s longest buildings; 122 years later, 210 feet were removed for a new bridge and its old bricks are being reused
articles.summary: US News: Longworth Hall, a historic railroad freight warehouse in Cincinnati, is now shorter than it was for most of its history. About 210 feet of the world’s.
articles.body: Longworth Hall, a historic railroad freight warehouse in Cincinnati, is now shorter than it was for most of its history. About 210 feet of the world’s longest buildings has been removed to make way for a new bridge over the Ohio River.The demolition is part of the Brent Spence companion bridge project. According to NPR, work on the new bridge officially began with a groundbreaking ceremony in May, and the removal of part of Longworth Hall has been one of the first visible changes linked to the project.The historic building at 700 W Pete Rose Way was completed in 1904 by the Baltimore & Ohio Railroad as a warehouse for rail freight. At the time, it was 1,227 feet long and was described as one of the longest buildings in the world.Most of Longworth Hall will remain standing, however. The section being removed is largely an addition constructed in the 1960s. According to the Cincinnati Enquirer, contractors took about six months to remove roughly one-fifth of the building. A time-lapse video also shows the demolition taking place in less than a minute.The building had shrunk beforeThe latest demolition is not the first time Longworth Hall has lost part of its length. In 1961, about 150 feet of the building was removed to make room for Interstate 75 on the Cincinnati side of the Ohio River. That section was later restored.Ironically, the part being removed now was itself added in the 1960s, after the building had already been shortened for the interstate.Longworth Hall has also changed ownership over the decades. In 1985, it was sold to Roy and Ron Schweitzer and Rudy Hermes, with the Schweitzers taking ownership soon afterwards. The building was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1986.In 2023, the Ohio Department of Transportation acquired the property. ODOT now owns the building and plans to put it up for sale after the new bridge is completed.The current work is being carried out carefully because the remaining structure is historic. While much of the 210-foot section is being demolished, a portion of the original building will be taken apart in a way that allows its old bricks to be saved.Old bricks will help rebuild the east endThe next stage will involve rebuilding Longworth Hall's east end with bricks recovered during the demolition. The work will also include cleaning the exterior, replacing deteriorating bricks and mortar, and improving the building's exterior windows.Other original materials left over from the demolition will also be saved for future maintenance and repairs.Ohio Department of Transportation Press Secretary Matt Bruning says, "The idea is that once all of this work is done, you will drive by on I-75 and look over at Longworth Hall and it will look like it did in 1904 when it was finished. Only it will be shorter," Bruning said.ODOT said the rebuilding of the east-facing wall is expected to be completed by the end of 2027. Demolition of the 1960s addition was expected to be completed within a couple of months, it was reported in March.Longworth Hall will also undergo extensive masonry work and upgrades to its historic windows before ODOT eventually transfers the property to its next owner.The new bridge behind changesThe changes to Longworth Hall are directly linked to the long-planned Brent Spence companion bridge. The new bridge is being built immediately west of the existing Brent Spence Bridge and will provide a new crossing over the Ohio River.The project is expected to cost almost $4.4 billion. That figure is higher than the $3.6 billion estimate given the previous year, before the final bridge design was selected.The bridge project will bring more visible construction activity around the area. Bruning said the work would eventually move into the river and towards the approaches to the bridge.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: One in eight young people not in work or education
articles.summary: Just under one million young people in the UK are not in education, employment or training (Neet).
articles.body:
Just under one million young people in the UK are not in education, employment or training - or "Neet" - according to data published ahead of a major report about a "lost generation".

The latest data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) suggests 981,000 people aged 16 to 24 were Neet between April and June. That is about one in eight people in that age group.

The final instalment of a major report by former minister Alan Milburn is expected to set out recommendations for tackling the problem in the coming weeks.

Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden told the BBC ministers would "take those [recommendations] forward".

Want your job application to stand out? Employers say they look for these six skills

Competition for degree apprenticeships quadruples as university costs rise

The new data suggests the number of young people who are Neet has fallen compared to the first three months of the year, when it was over one million, or 13.5% of the total population of people aged 16 to 24.

But it has risen by 3% compared to the same period last year, when it was 951,000 young people.

The estimates are based on information from a sample of households. The ONS says looking at a smaller subset, like Neets, leads to more "variability" - which can explain small changes from quarter to quarter and means it is best to look at long-term, rather than short-term, changes.

Asia Mason, 22, from London, says she spent more than two years applying for jobs before she finally secured her first role in the NHS.

After leaving college with a health and social care qualification, Mason hoped to work in maternity. She applied for more than 30 jobs but was repeatedly told she lacked experience.

"I remember thinking, 'How am I supposed to get experience if nobody is willing to give me the opportunity to gain it?'" she says.

She ended up securing her first NHS role after completing a social care programme run by The King's Trust charity, which helped her gain experience and confidence.

Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said the UK labour market was "in a robust position" but there had been "a long-term challenge for young people".

He said he was "looking forward" to recommendations on how to tackle the issue from Milburn.

"We'll have proposals, legislation, if necessary, to take those forward," he said.

McFadden spoke to the BBC during a visit to Boots in Nottingham, where young people had started jobs in a pilot of the government's Jobs Guarantee scheme.

Over the next three years, it aims to support 90,000 young people who have been claiming Universal Credit and looking for work for 18 months. It funds 25 hours of paid work every week for half a year.

McFadden said there were also plans for 300,000 more work experience placements and 50,000 more youth apprenticeship starts, adding that the government had already rolled out £3,000 hiring incentives for employers who take on young people who have been out of work for six months.

But shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately criticised the government's policies, claiming Labour had "destroyed job opportunities for young people" through increased taxes, such as employer National Insurance contributions .

For the Liberal Democrats, Munira Wilson said the sheer number of Neets represented a "generational betrayal", and said the government needed to make it "more attractive for businesses to take on apprentices, boosting the number of degree apprenticeships , and crucially, reversing Labour's damaging job tax".

The rise in the number of Neets between April and June compared to the same time last year was largely an increase among men.

An extra 25,000 men were estimated to be Neet, compared to another 4,000 young women.

In May, the first part of Milburn's report, which was commissioned by the government, said the reasons for the rise in rates among men were "complex", but could be down to more health issues, the "erosion of traditional employment routes" and "a growing gap in educational outcomes".

He also said the "Neet problem is grounded in social disadvantage" and highlighted higher rates among certain groups, including young people who:

have special educational needs or disabilities (SEND)

The report warned that one in six young people would be out of work in five years without action, adding: "We are at risk of a lost generation."

It said young jobseekers were submitting dozens, sometimes hundreds of applications, but rejections had become the norm.

Last week, analysis by the BBC found that competition for degree apprenticeships in England through the government's "find an apprenticeship" service, for example, had quadrupled over the past three years.

The second, and final, instalment of Milburn's report - including recommendations for how to tackle the problems - is expected in the coming weeks.

articles.title: I’m president of one of America’s most reliable allies. Here’s how we stand up to Russia
articles.summary: Romania pledges 5% GDP defense spending by 2035 and billions in Black Sea military infrastructure to strengthen NATO's southeastern flank against Russia.
articles.body: Russia is a growing threat that America and Europe cannot afford to ignore. Romanian airspace has been violated by drones dozens of times in recent months. According to press reports, American intelligence believes Russia may test NATO’s resolve with a limited move against an allied country. For Romania, none of this is abstract. We sit on NATO’s southeastern flank, on the Black Sea, and we share the longest border with Ukraine of any ally. We have watched this from its edge for years, with drones crossing into our airspace and debris falling on our territory. We have learned by direct experience that deterrence is tested first at the perimeter of the alliance. The partnership between Romania and the United States was built for moments like this. Its strength rests on two things: geography and reliability. Geography we did not choose. Reliability we have earned. When Operation Epic Fury required access and support, Romania was among the first allies to answer. Quickly and publicly. That is what a trusted partner does. US INTEL WARNS RUSSIA COULD LAUNCH LIMITED ATTACK ON NATO ALLY IN EFFORT TO FRAGMENT ORGANIZATION: REPORT That is why I recently sent our national security advisor and our chief of defense to convey Romania’s commitment to Black Sea security, to NATO burden-sharing and burden-shifting, and to deeper strategic partnership with the United States. I asked them to keep that conversation going, in Washington and at NATO headquarters, to answer whatever questions our American allies may have. And to make clear that Romania is prepared to raise both the level of its commitments and the speed at which it delivers them. Behind that offer lies a simple premise. Romania is not asking America for more. Romania is offering to do more. We are grateful for American leadership and understand that gratitude must be matched by responsibility. The United States is right to expect Europe to carry more of its own defense, and Romania is backing that expectation with money and action, including the benchmark of spending 5% of GDP on defense by 2035. AS TRUMP'S NATO GAMBLE PAYS OFF, ENVOY NAMES ALLIES HE'S STILL WATCHING At Mihail Kogălniceanu Air Base, on the Black Sea coast, Romania began one of the largest military infrastructure programs anywhere on NATO’s eastern flank: roughly €2.5 to €3 billion in expansion and modernization under way or planned. Câmpia Turzii, Cincu, Smârdan, Babadag, Constanța and the Danube are being connected through a military logistics network, linking airfields, roads, ports, training grounds and supply infrastructure so Romania and the United States can rapidly move troops and equipment when needed most. The modernization of our armed forces is anchored in American systems: Patriot air and missile defense, HIMARS rocket artillery, F-16s, Abrams tanks and 32 planned F-35As. This is not a shopping list. It is a decision to be interoperable with American and NATO platforms. And for Romanian forces to be ready on the first day of a crisis rather than the 30th. THE TWO MOST IMPORTANT AMERICAN WEAPONS SYSTEMS NATO IS EAGER TO HAVE Because deterrence is not only about what NATO can do once a crisis has begun. It is about persuading an adversary, before that moment arrives, that aggression will fail and that the alliance will answer as one. That requires visible capability, resilient infrastructure and the political will to use both. It also requires allies to know they can count on one another, not only in Washington or Brussels, but on the ground, where geography and readiness decide how fast a decision becomes an action. Europe’s answer to Russia includes Romanian runways, ports, training ranges, pipelines and air-defense batteries, as well as the support Romania provides its allies under pressure. A stronger Romania means a stronger southeastern flank. A stronger flank means a more secure Black Sea. And a more secure Black Sea strengthens NATO’s ability to deter conflict across the whole of Europe. articles.title: What does the Meta settlement mean for the UK? Five things we learned
articles.summary: Other social media firms are yet to respond, while the debate from campaigners is far from over.
articles.body:
Meta's $18bn (£13.3bn) settlement with nearly every US state is about more than money.

As part of the deal, Facebook and Instagram have agreed to bring in several significant measures to protect children online - though Meta has not admitted to any wrongdoing.

These include time limits, warnings over screen time and more parental controls over their children's accounts.

At the moment, they will just apply to children in the US - but they could have an impact on the rest of the world.

And if they ultimately set a precedent, other social media companies may be forced to take up the rules, too.

The UK has its own measures in place to protect children online.

The Online Safety Act mainly put restrictions on what content young people can see online.

But the UK government has gone further than the US ban already.

Earlier this year, it announced an outright social media ban for under-16s, which will take effect in 2027.

Some other measures will apply to 16 and 17-year-olds, such as curfews and restrictions during certain hours of the day .

The US has to some extent followed the same path: Start by policing the content on the platforms, then move on to restricting access to social media.

But the core difference is children in the US will not be banned completely.

Instead, they will not have access to Facebook and Instagram overnight, have to follow time limits, and there will be prompts for children who use them for a long time.

Unlike in the UK, these are not put in by law, and will only apply to the two platforms so far (more on that below).

The UK government said it was "following developments closely" in the Meta settlement.

But now those safety features have been accepted by Meta in the US, other countries may start asking for them too.

"These tech platforms don't usually do anything unless they are told to do it," said Trevor Johnson, a former senior figure at Meta and TikTok, who spoke to Radio 4's Today programme.

"But I do think the UK will feel empowered to at least ask for the same restrictions."

Another former Meta director, Zvika Krieger, said Meta agreed to the changes because it saw "the writing on the wall".

"They're trying to demonstrate, 'Oh, you don't need to go and do a complete ban'," he told 5 Live Breakfast.

"I think that they probably would roll out a lot of these features to the rest of the world as well."

Meta may have been the target in this court case, but it has tried to bring the rest of Big Tech into the firing line.

At the same time as announcing the settlement, Meta called on TikTok and YouTube to bring in the same measures.

A Meta spokesperson told Reuters the company was "hopeful" Snap would make similar changes too.

The tech firm has always argued for a level playing field when it comes to regulation - it doesn't want Facebook and Instagram to be more restricted than its rivals, which might be able to hoover up teens who want a freer experience online.

"All platforms should empower parents and support teens in these ways because we know that when teens are restricted on one app, they simply move to another," Meta said.

YouTube, Snapchat and TikTok have maintained they have robust children's safety policies in place.

"There will be pressure for those platforms to adopt similar restrictions," Johnson said.

But they may not come willingly. So far, almost 24 hours after the gauntlet was thrown down by Meta, none have made a public comment.

"Time and time again social media companies don't make changes until they're forced," Ellen Roome, whose son Jools died after taking part in an online challenge, told Today.

Roome is part of a group of parents suing TikTok in the US over child safety.

Meta will pay out up to $18bn to almost all US states, plus the District of Columbia and three US territories.

30% of that is dependent on TikTok and YouTube agreeing to put in child safety measures.

This is far less than the hundreds of billions being speculated ahead of the trial.

It is also a fraction of Meta's revenue of $201bn last year - and Meta will be paying out the money over the course of a decade.

But the firm's future revenue may be affected by a drop in users or younger users spending less time on their platforms.

The complainants will share the money, with different states getting different amounts - but they will get hundreds of millions of dollars each.

New York state, which will receive at least $819m according to its attorney general, said the money would be used "to support mental health services, education programs, and other efforts to repair and reduce the harm caused by unhealthy social media use among young people".

Many other states have said they have earmarked the cash for similar initiatives.

The only two US states not included are Florida, which rejected the settlement, and New Mexico, which was not included in the offer after a previous court cases resulted in a $942m fine .

What about the wider debate over online safety?

Former Meta whistleblower Arturo Béjar, who was a witness in the trial, cited the now-familiar comparison of social media with Big Tobacco .

But, he told the BBC, even after companies were found to be pushing harmful products, they "were still able to sell cigarettes and the cigarettes were still as harmful".

Alexa Knight from the Mental Health Foundation gave a different analogy - consumer products.

"We expect the manufacturers to make sure their products are safe before they're released... particularly when there are children using them," she told 5 Live Breakfast.

"And we think it should be the same way for Big Tech."

That is to say, campaigners like Béjar and Knight are not going away.

Roome also said the new measures in place were a start, but don't go far enough.

There will be time limits on app usage, she said, "but what about the content on the platform?"

No one is claiming the settlement is a silver bullet, but it's likely Meta and its fellow social media companies will continue to face scrutiny over the safety of children and adults on its platforms.

One of the issues which triggered this trial concerned how Meta collected and used the data of young people, including those aged under 13.

Social media companies collect vast amounts of data in order to target advertising, and also to work out what kind of content to show each user.

In the settlement agreement, Meta must only use young people's personal data to estimate their age.

If they are under 13, they should be kicked of the platforms, and if they are 13-17, they should be subject to the extra protections for children.

Meta said it would strengthen its age assurance technology to make sure these are robust.

And it reiterated its longstanding call for age verification to be carried out by app stores rather than by Meta itself.

But privacy campaigners have argued in the past that age verification methods require companies to take even more personal data from users.
